Product teardown · outside-in

Navi Personal Loan:
where the funnel spends effort
before it earns it.

The origination journey to the offer page, mapped screen by screen against Fibe and Moneyview — and the changes I'd ship and A/B test first. No conversion figures are used or implied; the funnel data is yours. Prepared as a work sample for the Navi PM role.

Shivam · ~2 yrs, lending origination & decisioning01
The argumentExecutive summary

Navi delivers value early — then front-loads effort at the exact moment it matters most.

A ₹20L pre-approval appears in seconds. But before the personalised offer, one flow — the same for everyone — demands a mandatory permissions wall, a hop into a browser, a hand-typed PAN, and a bank-statement pull. Each is a place to prefill, defer, or route around.

01

Identity is typed, not confirmed

Name, DOB and PAN keyed by hand in a webview. The data already exists in CKYCR — prefill it and ask "is this you?"

02

Effort comes before commitment

Permissions and a bank-statement pull sit ahead of the offer. Move consent to the OTP moment; route known employers around the AA flow entirely.

03

One flow for every borrower

Same screens for a salaried Cat-A applicant and a thin-file one. That's not a fault — it's untested upside. A/B routing is the unlock.

Method · 3 lenders mapped to the offer page · every claim framed as a hypothesis to test, never as a stated %02

Exhibit 1 · IdentityNow → Ship

Navi is the only one of the three that makes you type your PAN.

Navi today

  • Inside a navi.com webview, not the native app.
  • A typo = a hard stop one tap from the offer.

  • Zero fields typed. The consent to pull CKYCR/UIDAI is already collected one screen earlier — so show the PAN, don't ask for it.
  • Native — no browser hand-off, no typo dead-ends.
  • Peer proof · MoneyviewFibe auto-verifies

Why it pays: the PAN screen is the highest-effort, highest-abandon-risk step, one tap from the offer. Measure: completion + retry on this screen vs. the funnel; share of KYC already resolvable via CKYCR before asking.

Peer benchmark: Moneyview takes "name as per PAN card" + bureau consent and pulls identity silently — the PAN is never shown to the user.04
Exhibit 2 · Consent & permissionsNow → Ship

Ask for consent when the user is already committed — not at a cold wall.

Navi today
  • Location + SMS + Apps bundled as "all mandatory," up front — then OS prompts on top.
  • Copy leans on "fraud checks" and "we collect your data" — scary at the exact moment of doubt.
  • Asked before a real number exists. Likely a drop-off zone.
Ship · fold into the OTP moment

Verifying your number
You've just committed — the ideal moment to ask.
  • Move consent to OTP-verify (or just after PAN confirm) — the user is already declaring information, so continuation is highest here.
  • Reframe the copy to benefits, not "fraud" and "data collection."
  • A/B · at-OTP vs post-PAN placement

Why it pays: a cold, mandatory, fraud-flavoured wall before any value is a classic abandon point. Measure: grant + continuation by placement (at-OTP vs post-PAN vs today); watch that SMS/financial-signal coverage the models rely on doesn't fall.

Guardrail: if softer, later consent thins the SMS/AA signal for a segment, keep a firmer ask for thin-file profiles only.05
Exhibit 3 · Underwriting routesNow → Ship

Everyone is pushed down the bank-statement route — even when they don't need it.

Navi today · one route
  • Every applicant runs the Account-Aggregator + bank-statement pull — a salaried Cat-A employee and a thin-file borrower alike.
  • The AA OTP + statement fetch is heavy, and a plausible drop-off driver for low-risk users who don't need it.
  • The ₹20L teaser itself is good — the problem is the single path behind it.
Ship · route by employer category
WIREFRAME
Verify your work email
You work at a known employer — skip the bank statement.
Work email
shivam@<employer>.com
Verified · Cat A
Offer ready — no AA needed
See my offer
Cat B / C → lighter AA or full statement pull, by risk.
  • Segment by employer: Cat A (large / verifiable) → work-email OTP → instant offer; Cat B/C → step up to AA / full statements.
  • Cheapest, lowest-friction path for the lowest-risk users.
  • A/B · email-only vs AA for Cat-A

Why it pays: forcing your safest, most convertible segment through your heaviest verification is where good applicants leak. Measure: drop at AA-OTP + statement pull by employer category; approval & risk of the email-only Cat-A cohort vs. control.

Prior art: salary-linked and employer-category underwriting is well established in Indian PL — the lever here is offering it as a route, not the default for all.06
Exhibit 4 · The offer screenKeep · test

Navi's transparency leads — but one offer screen for everyone leaves upside on the table.

Navi today · keep
  • Fee split out — amount − charges − GST — with What/Why/How. A trust standard most lenders miss. Keep it.
  • But the same screen ships to every user — nothing is being tested.
Test · comparison-first layouts
  • For a rate-shopper, Moneyview's per-tenure EMI comparison (principal + interest, side by side) reads better than a single plan.
  • Stand up 2–3 offer variants and let data pick the winner — by segment.
  • A/B · single-plan vs comparisonBenchmark · RamFinCorp

The point: a credible teardown names strengths too — Navi's fee honesty is one. The gap isn't the screen; it's that there's one screen for everyone. Measure: offer-view → accept across layouts, split by segment (Cat-A / thin-file / rate-shopper).

Peer benchmarks: Moneyview (per-tenure EMI split) and RamFinCorp are worth standing up as offer-screen variants against Navi's current single-plan view.07
The recommendationResequence · then test

Value and identity first; effort only once it pays.

The pitch

I map and rebuild lending journeys for a living. This one took an afternoon and the public app.

  • At Lentra I've mapped 10+ PL & card journeys end-to-end (Federal, HDFC, HDBFS, Poonawalla, ABFL) and the decisioning behind them — the exact backend this role owns.
  • Everything here is outside-in. With your funnel data and the decisioning stack, the tests above are a sprint — and I'd run them by segment, not one flow for all.
  • The redesign isn't a slide — it's a working prototype, clickable to the offer page.
